background_rationale: Spent about three decades at distributor Core-Mark, rising from a regional sales manager through distribution-center and divisional operations roles to CEO, then ran field operations and served as COO at PFG after it acquired Core-Mark.

notable.summary: On being named CEO effective Jan. 1, 2026, succeeding George Holm, McPherson said he was "honored to step into the role of CEO at this exciting time for PFG."

In his first quarterly report as CEO, PFG lowered its fiscal 2026 outlook to $67.25-$68.25 billion in net sales, citing market dynamics, while reporting second-quarter net sales up 5.2% to $16.4 billion.

Reporting third-quarter results, McPherson pointed to market share gains and progress integrating recent acquisitions including Cheney Brothers, and said he expected accelerating sales and profit growth in fiscal 2027.
PFG reported fiscal 2026 net sales of $67.8 billion (up 7.2%) and issued fiscal 2027 guidance of $72.5-$73.0 billion in net sales.

personal_story.hook: Scott McPherson joined Core-Mark as a Portland sales manager in 1992 and now runs a food distributor with $67.8 billion in annual sales.
personal_story.summary: McPherson earned a business degree at Lewis & Clark College and an MBA at the University of Portland. In 1992 he started as a general and area sales manager at Core-Mark's Portland, Oregon distribution center, and over the next 26 years moved through corporate marketing, running the Fort Worth distribution center, divisional operations and corporate development before becoming Core-Mark's CEO in 2018. After Performance Food Group acquired Core-Mark, he oversaw PFG's field operations, became president and COO in 2025, and succeeded George Holm as CEO on Jan. 1, 2026.
